title: Arkansas Traveler
short: Traditional (American); credited to Sanf · G 4/4 · play it with every note lit.

blocks.html: A famous old fiddle tune, tied to a comic story of a lost traveler and a backwoods fiddler. The A part uses the alternating-thumb roll (T I T M) with the melody on the thumb; the B part runs down the scale with pull-offs on the 3rd and 2nd strings. In bar 7 the open 5th string plays the high G of the melody.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys or strings light up as each note sounds.

blocks.html: The piece: Fiddle tune, first published in 1847; played across the South ever since

sources.name: Melody checked note by note against “Arkansas Traveller” in Ryan’s Mammoth Collection (Boston, 1883; reissued as Cole’s 1000 Fiddle Tunes), as transcribed in ABC by John Chambers at MIT (trillian.mit.edu). Moved from D to G; the fiddle’s sixteenth notes are our eighth notes. The note on every beat matches that version (on the beat or an eighth after it); between the beats we keep most of the tune and fill the rest with roll notes. The pickup is left out. History from Wikipedia.
